newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan housing starts seen falling in 97/98--report.
newsitem.headline: Japan housing starts seen falling in 97/98--report.

text.p: Japan's housing starts are expected to fall by nine percent in fiscal 1997/98 after a sales tax rise in April puts an end to the present home-buying spree, a research report by the Housing Loan Corporation said on Friday.

The semi-government body said housing starts were expected to fall to 1.5 million starts, a drop of 9.2 percent. The body has forecast a rise of 11.6 percent in housing starts for the current fiscal year ending in March.
The forecasts were made on the presumptions that low interest rates would continue and land prices in large cities fall by more than four percent next fiscal year, the report said.

It said the expected fall was a reaction to high levels seen last year due to rebuilding after the 1995 Kobe earthquake and the current home-buying spree ahead of a consumption tax increase from April 1.
The tax is due to be increased from three to five percent.
The report also said, however, that low interest rate levels would continue to provide some support to the market.
